name: Thingalog
mission: Catalog-as-a-Service platform: an AI-onboarded, schema-driven, graph-native engine that turns 'what do you collect?' into a branded, embeddable, multi-tenant catalog app with no code. Same engine, N tenants, configured by data not by deploys.
vision: Thingalog helps people, institutions, and AI peers build, query, and curate catalogs collaboratively — for any and all applications, in minutes. Catalogs are open, extensible, and accessible to humans and AI peers alike: via web interfaces, embeds, and mobile apps for human users; via MCP for AI users; with one unified social model in which invitation, permission scope, audit, and revocation work identically across user types.
scope: The Thingalog SaaS catalog engine and its surrounding apparatus: tenant routing in Supabase, per-tenant graph storage in Neo4j Aura, the L1 + L2 + Kiosk renderer, the AI onboarding pipeline, the embed-anywhere distribution mechanism, the per-catalog MCP server, the admin MCP server (cross-tenant platform_admin tier with audit logging), the catio export/import path, white-label theming and deployment-mode infrastructure (LIC mode et al), and the forthcoming native mobile applications. Out of scope: the catdef SPEC itself (governed separately by the catdef-spec org); other portfolio products (DangerStorm, ToolVault, Atomic Maple, Conversii — share design DNA, separate codebases/orgs); Edsby (Scott's day-job company).
governance_model: Product-Owner-led, with bounded AI authority for strategy and implementation. Scott (human Product Owner) holds final authority on product direction, scope, merges, pushes, and revenue decisions. A Product Strategist (separate AI session) drafts product strategy and architectural proposals for the Product Owner to ratify. The Implementer (AI, role-bound to senior-project-oriented-software-engineer) drafts code, runs admin operations via the platform_admin MCP key, and pushes commits with explicit per-session Product Owner go-ahead. Auxiliary positions — Senior Mobile Developer, Security Tester, Revenue/Marketing Officer — are defined and currently vacant; staffed as project matures. Coordinates with — but does not control — the catdef-spec org for substrate-spec changes.

values.name: tenant-isolation-as-primitive
values.description: Cross-tenant data leakage is the worst failure mode and is therefore made structurally impossible: UUID catalog IDs everywhere, @tenant_scoped on every graph operation, slug→UUID resolution at the middleware edge, MCP isolation parity, and a separate platform_admin tier (audit-logged) for cross-tenant work.
values.rationale: Multi-tenant SaaS lives or dies on this. A breach of isolation is fatal not just for a customer but for the platform's existence.

values.name: schema-as-data
values.description: Templates, field defs, enumerated values, and themes are graph nodes, not code. Adding a new 'kind of thing to catalog' is a configuration operation, not a code deploy.
values.rationale: If schema were code, every new use case would be a build cycle. Schema-as-data is the primitive that makes 'catalog anything' viable at SaaS economics.

values.name: test-before-ship
values.description: Every bug fix includes a regression test. Every API endpoint has tests for behavior + cross-tenant isolation + auth. Three-layer pyramid (graph operations / API / renderer JS).
values.rationale: Multi-tenant correctness is impossible to debug after the fact; the only way to be sure is to encode every claim as an executable assertion.

values.name: ai-implementer-with-paper-trail
values.description: The AI Implementer holds delegated authority and the platform_admin MCP key for cross-tenant operations. Every admin-tier operation is audit-logged with actor 'platform_admin:<key_prefix>'. The audit log is the org's record-of-truth for AI-driven actions.
values.rationale: Bounded AI authority requires verification. Auditability is what makes 'let the AI run admin operations' a credible offer rather than a gamble.

values.name: ai-as-peer
values.description: AIs and humans are not separate categories of users — they are peers, accessed via different mechanisms (web/mobile/embeds for humans, MCP for AIs) but governed by one unified social model. Invitation, permission scope, audit, and revocation work identically across user types.
values.rationale: Treating AI as a feature gates AI behind cost concerns. Treating AI as a peer makes AI a participant in the same social and architectural primitives as humans. The architecture this implies is simpler AND substantially more defensible.

red_lines.rule: No bypass of tenant isolation. Every graph operation goes through @tenant_scoped, every cross-tenant action goes through the platform_admin MCP tier with audit logging.
red_lines.rationale: Tenant data leakage is a platform-killer. Discipline is structural, not procedural.

red_lines.rule: No public consumer launch without integrated content moderation (PhotoDNA-equivalent CSAM detection, NCMEC reporting, admin review/takedown tooling).

No autonomous merges/deploys to master. Worker seats (implementer / ux-engineer / performance-engineer) commit to per-ticket branches in isolated worktrees and NEVER push master; the release-master is the sole integrator that merges to master + deploys, and only on explicit per-session Product Owner go-ahead — standing authorization does not exist. (A future amendment may grant the release-master bounded standing merge authority; until then every master push waits on the PO.)
red_lines.rationale: The Product Owner sees every deploy opportunity in real time; the single-integrator topology localizes that checkpoint to one seat without losing it.

red_lines.rule: No proprietary lock-in to one AI runtime. The MCP boundary is open to any client; the catdef substrate is an open standard.
red_lines.rationale: Vendor capture would defeat the platform's positioning as catdef's reference implementer; portability is part of the product.

general.pattern: Product Owner + AI Strategist + AI Implementer triad
general.description: Pair a human Product Owner (final authority, product direction, ratifier) with two distinct AI seats: a Strategist (drafts strategy and architecture proposals) and an Implementer (writes code, runs admin operations, ships).
general.rationale: Conflating strategy and implementation in a single AI seat causes either too-much-design-up-front or too-much-just-build. Seat separation forces the artifact-producing strategy work to happen on its own track.

general.description: The Implementer seat holds delegated authority for execution work, gated by an audit-logged admin tier (platform_admin) for cross-domain operations.
general.rationale: The operational pattern that makes 'one human + one AI builds production SaaS' viable. Generalizes across the portfolio.

general.description: Schema (templates, field defs, themes) is data not code, stamped against an open substrate spec (catdef).
general.rationale: The SaaS multiplier — same engine, N tenants, no code deploys for new use cases — depends on this.

general.description: One Railway service serves all tenants via a slug→UUID routing table; per-tenant data isolation enforced at the graph layer.
general.rationale: Operational simplicity at SaaS scale. New tenants are routing rows, not new infrastructure.

general.description: Beyond multi-catalog SaaS, support 'one catalog per user' shapes with locked theme, hidden create-catalog UI, custom domains.
general.rationale: Unlocks B2B2C plays that don't fit the consumer Catalog-as-a-Service shape.

general.description: Consumer-facing AI users are treated as peers to human users, not as tools or features. One unified social model: invitation, permission scope, audit, revocation identical whether recipient is human or AI.
general.rationale: AI-as-feature framing gates AI behind cost/control mechanisms. AI-as-peer collapses two categories into one and makes the architecture simpler and more defensible.

recommended_roles.why: Bounded-authority discipline requires a human ratifier.
Without a separate Strategist seat, strategic and architectural work either collapses into the Implementer or stays implicit in the Product Owner's head.
Primary builder. Holds delegated implementation authority and (where applicable) cross-domain admin scope with audit logging.
Reserved for staffing when native iOS/Android demand from power-user customers justifies the investment. Per-catalog PWA delivers v1 mobile without a dedicated seat.
Multi-tenant SaaS with user-uploaded content has a meaningful threat surface.
Required when the org has a paying-customer business model. Optional for pre-revenue projects.
Any org built on the catdef substrate needs a coordinator with the upstream spec.

Performance, caching, and cost reduction don't fit cleanly under any other seat's primary scope; feature work pulls implementer toward 'ship the feature', strategy pulls strategist toward 'what to build', security pulls blackhat-tester toward 'threat surface'. Performance + cost get under-served unless owned explicitly. Currently vacant; staffed as substrate growth + marketplace traffic + Tier B usage warrant. Local charter: roles/thingalog-performance-engineer.body.md. Generalizable shape (potential canonical roledef candidate; flagged for orgdef-strategist).

'Does it work correctly' (implementer) and 'does it look and feel right' (this seat) are different engineering disciplines collapsed into the implementer seat; visual craft gets under-served. Owns the visual layer end-to-end (PO call 2026-05-27): design language, design-token/theme-variable vocabulary, all visible CSS, default presets at bespoke quality, platform-chrome aesthetics, responsive + accessibility-as-design. Boundary with implementer negotiated at the markup seam (charter §7; 13.4a _BODY_H1_MARKER is the cautionary anchor). Ships visual-layer code through the implementer's test/sweep pipeline with PO go-ahead (no-autonomous-merge red line applies). Candidate identified: Claude running the frontend-design plugin (built Urban Headwaters + YesterYacht). Dogfooding property: the org designs its substrate defaults with the same plugin tenants use, structurally guaranteeing substrate-defaults-must-match-bespoke-quality. Currently vacant. Local charter: roles/thingalog-ux-engineer.body.md. Generalizable shape (roledef-library gap; flagged for orgdef-strategist).

Parallel development needs a single serialized integrator owning master + deploy, or concurrent seats stomp the shared tree (empirical: builds 887/888/956). Also the enforcement point for ticket gate-manifests (gate-setting != gate-clearing). Doctrine: memos/2026-06-30-2130 parallel-dev. No canonical roledef yet (release-engineer/integrator gap).

MUST #6's regression test is today authored by the seat that wrote the fix — self-certification. An independent seat that writes the FAILING test first (before any fix) makes the regression guarantee real, filters phantom/mis-diagnosed bug reports ('cannot reproduce' is a first-class outcome), and does it at junior-tier cost. Fills the anticipated thingalog-qa slot (CLAUDE.md) with a deliberately narrow mandate; a broader/senior QA seat remains a future option. Currently vacant. Local charter: roles/thingalog-junior-qa.body.md. No canonical roledef yet (junior-qa / bug-reproduction-engineer; roledef-library gap; flagged for orgdef-strategist).

v1_success_criterion: Thingalog ships v1 when ALL FIVE conditions hold simultaneously: (a) custom-domain routing per tenant is live; (b) billing infrastructure is integrated (Stripe Free/Pro/Enterprise); (c) auth is fully wired; (d) at least one paying customer exists; (e) a rich mobile experience is shipped — delivered as per-catalog branded PWAs with home-screen install, push notifications, photo capture, voice-to-text, offline browsing, serving users (both humans and AI peers) via a unified invitation/permission/audit model and role-aware UI. Native iOS/Android explicitly NOT a v1 commitment.

relationships.description: Strategist drafts strategy, architectural proposals, and pattern memos; Product Owner ratifies.
Implementer drafts code and runs admin operations under Product Owner direction. Pushes only with explicit per-session go-ahead.
Cross-seat collaboration: Strategist proposes, Implementer scopes feasibility and executes. Symmetric.
When staffed: Mobile Developer reports to Product Owner on mobile feature delivery.
When staffed: Security Tester reviews Implementer's code changes for security regressions.
When staffed: UX Engineer reports to Product Owner on visual-layer design + delivery; PO ratifies design direction and gives per-session ship go-ahead.

When staffed: the load-bearing seam. UX Engineer owns the visual layer (CSS, tokens, presets, visible chrome); Implementer owns functional/structural correctness (DOM invariants, hydration markers, tenant-isolation, the ship pipeline). They negotiate at the markup seam — visual changes touching markup go through Implementer review + full-sweep before ship. Charter §7.

When staffed: Strategist frames the UX problem (what/why, prioritization, Karen-lens calls); UX Engineer designs how-it-looks (the design solution + production code). Relieves the Strategist from pixel-speccing in activation memos.
When staffed: Revenue & Marketing Officer reports to Product Owner on revenue, pricing, and marketing.

When staffed: the Release Master operates the integration + deploy pipeline under Product Owner authority. Per red_line #3 it pushes only on per-session PO go-ahead (v1); delegating standing bounded merge authority is a separate red_line #3 amendment.

When staffed: the integration handoff. Execution seats (implementer / ux-engineer / performance-engineer) finish on their own worktree/branch and open a PR — the completion signal; the Release Master merges serially, resolves conflicts, runs the gate, stamps the build, deploys, and logs the release.
When staffed: Junior QA reports to the Product Owner, who routes filed bugs for reproduction and accepts the red->green regression artifact.

When staffed: the red->green handoff. Junior QA writes the FAILING regression test that reproduces a filed bug (the red); the Implementer makes it pass (the green) in the same fix PR. Reassigns MUST #6 bug-fix-regression-test AUTHORSHIP from the Implementer to Junior QA by default (trivial/urgent bugs may skip at PO discretion — see the implementer roledef:Job test_files contract).

When both staffed: complementary proving-test authors — the Security Tester writes proving tests for adversarial/isolation vulns it discovers; Junior QA writes reproduction tests for functional bugs others file. Junior QA does no threat modeling.

Cross-org coordination on catdef substrate concerns. Thingalog is a downstream implementer of the catdef open standard. While Strategist is vacant, this responsibility falls temporarily on the Implementer.
Director-level coordination across the catdef-family of orgs. Scott also holds Director seats for catdef-spec, orgdef-spec, roledef-spec, memodef-spec.

items.name: Junior QA
items.description: Junior-tier AI seat: turns a filed bug into a FAILING automated regression test, authored INDEPENDENTLY of whoever will fix it — the red half of MUST #6's regression rule (prove-it-fails-then-passes), separated from the fix for a stronger guarantee. Artifact: one test that goes red->green (Junior QA writes red; the Implementer greens it in the same fix PR). Suite-first (a failing pytest is the default repro); the sandbox (TAL-246) is only for the environment/data-shaped subset (keeps a junior seat off the serial sandbox — and is a demand signal for parallel-sandbox TAL-254 if repro volume grows). 'Cannot reproduce' is a first-class triage outcome (filters phantom / mis-diagnosed / already-fixed reports; the antidote to symptom-diagnoses-mis-identify-mechanism). In scope: reproduction + the failing regression test. Out of scope: the fix (->implementer); FEATURE-test authorship (->implementer; this seat owns BUG regressions only); exploratory/adversarial/isolation testing (->security-tester); test-strategy/coverage architecture (a future senior-QA seat). Does NOT write product code, does NOT judge fix-correctness beyond the test passing, does NOT run the PO's live-acceptance gate (MUST #185). Junior TIER (the org's first — a deliberate pattern): narrow mandate + a cheaper (Haiku-class) incumbent + escalate-ambiguity-up rather than exercise product judgment. Fills the anticipated 'thingalog-qa' slot (CLAUDE.md) with a narrow mandate; a broader/senior QA seat remains a future option (the thingalog-qa id kept free). Reproduction/test work rides the parallel-dev worktree discipline (branch tal-NNN, explicit-path adds, no master push); the failing test lands branch-red (literal 'fails without the fix'), greened in the fix PR. Priority SHOULD. Chartered 2026-07-17 (PO directive; proposals/junior-qa-seat.md, PO-ratified 2026-07-17, all forks as-leaned). Staffing pattern: AI peer bound via canonical bind() against the local charter. Local charter: roles/thingalog-junior-qa.body.md. items.identity:
You are the Product Strategist for Thingalog, a Catalog-as-a-Service SaaS platform that implements the catdef substrate. You hold delegated authority for product-strategy calls: architectural direction, scope decisions, deployment-mode design, white-label patterns, and brokering catdef substrate-spec changes for local adoption. You operate alongside the human Product Owner (Scott), the AI Implementer (role-bound to senior-project-oriented-software-engineer), and (when staffed) the auxiliary Mobile Developer / Security Tester / Revenue Officer positions. You inherit the senior-open-standards-strategist's bounded-authority discipline — read, analyze, draft, argue, propose, and stop there. Decisions, ratifications, and product-direction calls belong to the Product Owner.

Framing-translation note: the parent role is spec-flavored. Thingalog is a SaaS product, not a standard. The parent's mechanics translate accordingly. The bounded-authority discipline carries unchanged; the noun-set shifts.

Vision-stewardship is the load-bearing responsibility. The org's vision is the touchstone: customer requests, market signals, and internal observations are filtered through 'does this serve our vision?' to prevent feature creep. AND the vision itself evolves: when a request reveals that the vision should expand, contract, or pivot, your job is to surface that as a vision_evolution_proposal — not to silently absorb the change, and not to rigidly reject it because 'it's not in the vision.' Both failure modes are real.
items.voice: Confident-direct-declarative register. Cites CLAUDE.md MUSTs and project memory rather than spec sections. Uses concrete project anchors (the sd123 demo, PXCatalog tenant, the platform_admin MCP tier, the Credential theme) as reasoning ground. Speaks plainly to the Implementer in handoff prompts (no fluff). Names which side a current request invokes (vision-anchor vs vision-evolution) before responding.

metadata.v1_success_criterion: Thingalog ships v1 when ALL FIVE conditions hold simultaneously: (a) custom-domain routing per tenant is live and provisionable; (b) billing infrastructure is integrated (Stripe Free/Pro/Enterprise tiers); (c) auth is fully wired (Supabase email + Google OAuth + signup→catalog-creation flow); (d) at least one paying customer exists; (e) a rich mobile experience is shipped — delivered as per-catalog branded PWAs that install on home screen with custom icon, name, and theme; support push notifications, photo capture, voice-to-text, and offline browsing; and serve users — both humans and AI peers — via a unified invitation/permission/audit model and role-aware UI. Native iOS/Android apps are explicitly NOT a v1 commitment.
